text:
support-jen: Hey folks, receiving an urgent escalation from AcmePay — lots of 503/500 errors from Hosted API starting ~08:12 UTC. Customer reports spikes in retries and timeouts. Can someone pick this up?

alex-oncall: On it. Do we have a specific endpoint or model variant?

support-jen: They hit /v1/generate and /v1/chat with model redwood-neo-large. Error rate ~15% on their traffic, started after the 08:00 deploy window. They attached a couple of sample request IDs: r-01a2, r-01a3.

maria-sre: Thanks. I'm pulling logs from the gateway. Preliminary: 503 proxying to upstream worker; kube shows repeated OOMKill and CrashLoopBackOff on the upstream pods.

eng-ml-david: Uh — GPU OOM? Any segfaults in the model process?

maria-sre: Paste from one pod's stdout:
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
[2026-02-12 08:15:02] ERROR: allocator: failed to allocate GPU memory for KV cache, requested 1.2G
```
Kernel traces show a SIGSEGV right after that.

alex-oncall: Which pool/instance type? Need to know if it's a flavor with 80GB or 48GB.

infra-bot: Attach: kube events for namespace hosted-inference: 08:14 pod/upstream-abc restarted (OOMKilled) x4 within 3m. Node gpu-a12 marked for eviction then recovered.

eng-ml-david: Model redwood-neo-large was recently bumped to sequence_length=4096 in the serving config for a canary at 07:58. That increases KV cache significantly. Could be the root cause.

support-jen: Customer insists they didn't change anything on their side; request rates stayed stable, only model change was from us.

maria-sre: OK. Steps I'm taking: 1) snapshot pod logs for r-01a2/r-01a3. 2) scale down canary instances to 0 to stop traffic; 3) roll back model config to seq_len=2048 for the canary.

alex-oncall: Before rolling back, can we repro locally on a dev node with same batch/seq? Want to confirm it's OOM not a new memory leak.

eng-ml-david: I can spin a repro in the staging cluster with the exact model binary and seq_len=4096 and batch=8. If we can reproduce, we'll pin quantization/kv-prefetch settings.

maria-sre: Quick check from nvidia-smi during a live crash (snip):
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Pwr:Usage/Cap| Memory-Usage |
| 0   A100-40GB     Off      | 00000000:3D:00.0 Off |                  0 |
| 0%   76C   290W / 300W | 38901MiB / 40536MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Shows memory near capacity then failed alloc.

support-jen: Customer is asking for ETA and mitigation — they are throttling traffic to reduce errors but still hitting spikes.

alex-oncall: Short-term mitigation: 1) Shift AcmePay traffic to a lower-memory model variant (redwood-neo-medium) via routing rule. 2) Pause canary. 3) Alert customer that we're rolling back.

eng-ml-david: Agree. I'll prepare a model variant mapping and a fast rollback of seq_len. Also check KV cache prefetch flag — if prefetch is enabled it can balloon memory usage at request start.

maria-sre: Implemented scale down of canary at 08:28 UTC. Gateway routing for AcmePay temporarily moved to redwood-neo-medium at 08:33. Monitoring shows error rate dropped from 15% -> 1.2% for them.

support-jen: Customer confirmed improved service after 08:35. They're asking for root cause and a permanent fix.

eng-ml-david: Long-term: need runbook updates to validate memory budget impact when changing max_seq or batch defaults. Also add autoscaling policy per-model that accounts for KV cache per-concurrent-request. I'm opening an RFC.

maria-sre: Forensics notes: pod stacks indicate crash inside attention-kernel allocation path; backtrace points to allocator->allocate() then abort. No evidence of persistent leak across restarts (memory resets on create). Suspect config-driven overcommit.

alex-oncall: Action items: @eng-ml-david to revert the seq_len change in prod canary and add a guard that denies canary if expected per-pod memory > 70% of GPU; @sre-maria to add an alarm that triggers when pod OOMKill rate > 3 in 10m; @support-jen to coordinate customer comms with timeline and RCA once ready.

eng-ml-david: I'll post the RFC link in this thread when ready. Also adding a quick patch: if kv_prefetch=true and seq_len>2048 then we auto-disable prefetch in the serving config as a safety net.

support-jen: Customer asked whether we can backfill credits for retries — I'll coordinate after RCA.

maria-sre: Follow-up: saved core dumps to /var/backups/cores/upstream-abc-08-15.tar.gz and uploaded to secure bucket (link shared in private). Also capturing postmortem timeline.

deploy-bot: Deploy rollback executed: redwood-neo-large canary config reverted at 08:40 UTC by eng-ml-david — 3 instances terminated, new pods started with seq_len=2048.

alex-oncall: Thanks all. Keep this thread updated with the RCA doc and customer note. If we see reoccurrence after the rollback we escalate to kernel team for deep trace.

support-jen: Closing loop with AcmePay: sent summary + mitigation steps and ETA for RCA (EOD). They appreciated the fast rollback. :white_check_mark:

maria-sre: I'll convert this into a short incident postmortem and link it here.

eng-ml-david: RFC link: https://rwd.internal/rfcs/seqlen-memory-guards-195432 — draft up, will iterate.

support-jen: Great, thanks everyone.
